title: Long-lived stream stalls from proxy/TLS lifecycle — runtime guard, SDK guidance, and customer bridge
creator: Roxanne Li
description: Multiple customers reported high rates of 5xx/timeout errors during long-lived streaming sessions (SSE / chunked responses). Initial triage found correlation with prolonged TLS session lifecycles and intermittent proxy-side TLS renegotiation on the edge path. When the renegotiation window overlapped with a client-initiated keepalive gap, connections would stall, the frontdoor would reset and cause upstream retries to cascade into tenant-visible 5xx spikes. This ticket tracks the targeted runtime guard, SDK guidance, short-term customer bridge and a safe rollout to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: Start a sustained streaming session using the standard SDK with chunked responses and a 10s client ping interval
Run a scaled client emulator (50 concurrent streams) behind the edge proxy with TLS session timeout set artificially low (to reproduce)
Observe streaming stalls after TLS session renegotiation attempt; capture nginx/edge logs, tcpdump and server-side goroutine stacks
Replay with SDK backoff disabled to see retry amplification and measure 5xx rate on hosted API dashboard
analysis_summary: Root cause: transient TLS session lifecycle events on the edge path can cause libssl renegotiation that blocks the socket read loop for up to socket-level timeout window (~4-6s) under certain kernel schedulers. The runtime's streaming worker assumed progress whenever the socket was writable and did not surface a short-term stalled-read state, so upstream callers retried immediately. Amplified by client SDKs that perform immediate fast retries without jitter, the result showed tenant-scoped 5xx/timeouts and service-wide incident noise. Secondary contributors: some customers use aggressive OS TCP keepalive defaults and there was no server-side application heartbeat for streaming responses.
proposed_fix: 1) Runtime: add a streaming read stall detector (lightweight watchdog per connection) that surfaces a 3s stalled-read metric and triggers a graceful half-close or soft-reset path rather than allowing callers to observe a hard 5xx. 2) Edge: increase TLS renegotiation safety window and disable opportunistic renegotiation on affected edge fleet during rollout. 3) SDK: publish updated backoff guidance and ship a minor SDK patch that adds randomized exponential backoff + per-request idempotency token recommendation for streaming reconnects. 4) Customer bridge: for the most affected tenants, enable tenant-level short-circuit that routes long-lived streams to a warmed pool with extended keepalive settings.
rollout_plan: Merge runtime guard PR to main - feature gated under feature flag runtime.streaming_stall_guard
Canary deploy to a single region with 5% of traffic (runtime-rc tag)
Enable edge safety window change behind ops switch for same canary region
Monitor metrics for 48 hours (stall_metric, streaming_5xx_rate, retry_amplification_index)
Progressively increase to 25%, 60% and full over 5 business days if stable
Coordinate SDK patch release and send advisory to affected customers during canary stage
qa_checks: Automated integration test: sustained 30-minute multi-stream session under simulated renegotiation event
Chaos: induce delayed TLS handshake during stream and verify stalled-read is handled without 5xx to caller
Load test: 500 concurrent streams against canary; verify no CPU regression >5% and no increase in tail latency
End-to-end: confirm SDK reconnect behavior with new backoff avoids retry storms in replay scenario

If this mitigates incidents but stalls persist, follow-up ticket will explore kernel-level socket scheduling knobs and decreased TLS renegotiation frequency service-wide.
